issues.title: Unqualified convergence to the barycenter

failure_location.quote: This gives rise to a computationally tractable stochastic fixed-point algorithm which is provably convergent to the 2-Wasserstein barycenter.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the operator~$G$ in (\ref{eqn: G-operator}) does not always have a unique fixed-point for general input probability measures

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the advertised computationally tractable algorithm is provably convergent to the 2-Wasserstein barycenter for the general class under discussion. The old paper actually proves only that accumulation points are fixed points of G, with barycenter convergence conditional on G having a unique fixed point. Because the paper also states that G can have additional fixed points and that uniqueness is open for non-parametric inputs, the unconditional headline guarantee materially exceeds the formal result.
issues.overall_effect: The headline contribution overstates the guarantee for general continuous non-parametric inputs: absent fixed-point uniqueness, the algorithm is not proved to converge to the barycenter and may accumulate at another fixed point.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unconditional headline claim by the precise guarantee that the iterates are almost surely precompact and every accumulation point is a fixed point of G, and that almost-sure convergence to the Wasserstein barycenter holds only when G has a unique fixed point. Apply the same qualification wherever the contribution is summarized.
issues.why_classification: Fixed-point uniqueness is known to fail in general and is unresolved for the advertised nonparametric regime. Qualifying the prose therefore withdraws the central unconditional general-input convergence guarantee, which is major mathematical loss; preserving that guarantee would require an essentially new global-optimality or fixed-point-uniqueness theorem.

issues.title: Missing bounded-density hypothesis in the G-operator theorem
issues.failure_explanation: Under the old assumptions, the invocation of the unique-barycenter result does not provide the asserted membership of the barycenter in P_{2,ac}, and the density-control step needed to keep limits inside the domain of G lacks its premise. Thus the imported fixed-point and accumulation theorem is stated outside the bounded-density regime supplied by the paper's own supporting result.
issues.overall_effect: The standalone G-operator theorem is not justified for arbitrary absolutely continuous inputs. Later uses inside the compact admissible class already have bounded densities, so the main algorithmic chain does not suffer an additional scope loss from this repair.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to the G-operator theorem the hypothesis that at least one input measure has an L-infinity-bounded density, so that the cited result supplies an absolutely continuous barycenter in the domain of G. No downstream restriction is needed because the compact admissible inputs used later already have bounded densities.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine missing premise rather than a transcription error, but the premise is stated in the paper's supporting barycenter theorem and is satisfied throughout the operative algorithmic regime. The short local correction preserves the method, conclusions, and downstream guarantees without meaningful loss.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: where for at least one index $k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$, $\nu_k$ has $\CL^{\infty}$-bounded density.

issues.title: Insufficient boundary regularity for global Brenier regularity

failure_location.quote: both have $\CC^2$-boundaries and are both uniformly convex

issues.failure_explanation: The old restatement of Caffarelli global regularity permits merely C2 boundaries for every q while concluding C^{q+2,alpha} regularity up to the boundary. This omits boundary smoothness needed at the claimed order. The curvature lemma then invokes that overbroad statement for the old admissible class, whose supports likewise have only C2 boundaries.
issues.overall_effect: High-order Brenier regularity and the resulting curvature and entropic-estimator consistency chain are not established for q at least one over the old admissible support class.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each q, require the source and target supports in the global Caffarelli theorem to have C^{q+2} boundaries, redefine the q-admissible support and measure classes accordingly, and propagate that strengthened support hypothesis through the curvature lemma, entropic-estimator proposition, and entropic convergence corollary.
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained and leaves the proofs, conclusions, and rates intact, so no global reconstruction is required. However, it narrows the entire affected chain from all uniformly convex C2 supports to higher-order smooth supports; C2-but-not-C^{q+2} domains form a coherent advertised regime rather than an exceptional degeneracy. The surviving chain is comparable but substantively restricted, making the issue moderate.

issues.title: Impossible midpoint definition of uniform convexity

failure_location.quote: is said to be uniformly convex if for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exists $\delta > 0$ such that, for any $\BIx, \BIy \in \CX$ with $\|\BIx - \BIy\| < \epsilon$, the distance from the mid-point $(\BIx + \BIy)/2$ to $\boundary(\CX)$ is at least $\delta$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: is said to be uniformly convex if for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exists $\delta > 0$ such that, for any $\BIx, \BIy \in \CX$ with $\|\BIx - \BIy\| < \epsilon$, the distance from the mid-point $(\BIx + \BIy)/2$ to $\boundary(\CX)$ is at least $\delta$.
A concrete example of such a family of increasing sets is $\big(\bar{B}(\veczero_d,r)\big)_{r\in\N}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The footnote claims that the displayed midpoint condition defines uniform convexity. Its actual consequence is that no nonempty open support is admissible, because x=y is allowed and can be chosen arbitrarily close to the boundary. This directly conflicts with the paper's assertion that closed balls provide a family of admissible increasing sets; the intended nonempty uniformly convex geometry and the literal empty geometry are materially different.
issues.overall_effect: Read literally, the admissible support class and the required increasing family are empty, so the concrete algorithm has no inputs of the advertised kind and its applicability discussion collapses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the midpoint criterion to require that the two points satisfy ||x-y|| at least epsilon, rather than ||x-y|| less than epsilon, while retaining the stated uniform lower bound on the midpoint's distance from the boundary.
issues.why_classification: The displayed clause is the standard midpoint formulation with its comparison reversed. Allowing x=y makes the printed version immediately impossible, while the conventional meaning of uniform convexity and the explicit closed-ball example uniquely force the corrected comparison. No proof or construction relies on the impossible literal reading.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: is said to be uniformly convex if its second fundamental form is uniformly positive on the whole of $\boundary(\CX)$

issues.title: Adaptive algorithm lacks a measurable construction
issues.failure_explanation: The adaptive algorithm requires the random radii, truncated measures, and pushforward measures to be measurable functions of the current state. The old source establishes only that suitable radii exist for each state and does not prove that the truncation and pushforward operations are Borel on the measure spaces. Consequently, the declared adapted stochastic process and the subsequent conditional expectations are not justified.
issues.overall_effect: The prescribed adaptive procedure is not established to define an adapted stochastic process, undermining the conditional-expectation decrement and the almost-sure convergence chain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Give explicit measurable choices of the truncation radii, for example as the least integers satisfying the tail bounds proved in the truncation lemma; prove that truncation of the current measure and pushforward by the estimated map are Borel operations on the relevant Wasserstein and function spaces; and then inductively establish adaptedness of the measure process before invoking the decrement proposition and both convergence results.
issues.why_classification: Pointwise existence of suitable radii does not provide the measurable selections needed for conditional expectations. Completing the construction requires contained but nontrivial measurable-selection and Borel-mapping lemmas, so it exceeds routine local bookkeeping. Those lemmas preserve the algorithm, hypotheses, and full affected convergence chain, avoiding both global reconstruction and mathematical loss.

issues.title: Missing minus signs make the convergence-proof tail divergent
issues.failure_explanation: The positive-exponent tail in the rearranged residual bound is infinite and cannot tend to zero, so the printed argument does not prove that the fixed-point residual vanishes along a convergent subsequence. The prior display already contains the required negative exponent, making the failure a propagated transcription error rather than a substantive flaw in the argument.
issues.overall_effect: As printed, the key step proving that every accumulation point is a fixed point fails, and the entropic convergence corollary consequently lacks its final convergence justification.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing minus sign in every copied tail after the rearrangement, replacing 10(s+1)^{1+beta} by 10(s+1)^{-(1+beta)}. The resulting convergent tail tends to zero and restores the fixed-point and entropic-corollary conclusions.
issues.why_classification: The immediately preceding display already has the correct negative exponent, and the subsequent statement that the tail vanishes uniquely forces the same exponent in the copied expressions. Correcting it changes no inference or construction and lets the printed argument proceed verbatim.

issues.title: Computational convergence wording blurs exact and numerical Sinkhorn solves

failure_location.quote: Consequently, using $\widehat{T}_{\mathrm{entr}}[\theta]$ as the OT map estimator in Algorithm~\ref{algo: iteration} results in a computationally tractable and efficient algorithm for Wasserstein barycenter that is also provably convergent.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for every $\theta>0$, let $(\widehat{f}^\theta_{i})_{i=1:m}$, $(\widehat{g}^\theta_{j})_{j=1:n}$ be the optimal solution of the dual entropic optimal transport problem:

Sinkhorn's algorithm is scalable to large sample sizes and admits highly parallelizable implementations on GPUs; see, e.g., \citep[Section~4.3]{peyre2019computational} for the numerical aspects of Sinkhorn's algorithm, and \citep{Feydy2019Fast} for a multiscale extension. In our numerical experiments, we utilize the Optimal Transport Tools (OTT) Python toolbox developed by \citet{cuturi2022optimal} to solve (\ref{eqn: OTmap-estimator-entropic-Sinkhorn}).

issues.failure_explanation: The estimator proposition explicitly uses an exact optimal dual solution. That supports a conventional reading in which the convergence result concerns exact optimisation subproblems. However, the computational remark moves directly from Sinkhorn, GPU implementations and the OTT experiments to the conclusion that the tractable algorithm is also provably convergent. It does not distinguish the exact-solve theoretical scheme from a numerically stopped Sinkhorn implementation. A reasonable reader can therefore mistake the convergence statement for a guarantee covering the implementation and its stopping error. The established defect is this unclear qualification; no failure of a finite implementation or of the exact-estimator result is established here.
issues.overall_effect: The computational discussion leaves the scope of the convergence guarantee misleadingly unclear. The exact-solution definition and the intended theoretical setting remain explicit in the formal results; this issue does not independently invalidate them.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State in the computational remark that the cited convergence result is for the estimator with exact dual optimisers, and distinguish this from finite-tolerance Sinkhorn implementations, whose additional optimisation error is not covered by that result. Keep the numerical experiments as empirical evidence. Align any wording that directly identifies the practical implementation with this theoretical guarantee. A finite-iteration error analysis would support a further implementation theorem, but is not required to repair this formulation issue.
issues.why_classification: Minor: the necessary exact-solve scope is already stated in the estimator definition, so an explicit local qualification resolves the misleading connection between computation and theory without changing the estimator, its stated assumptions or its convergence conclusion. The wording has more than one reasonable reading and is not a uniquely forced typo. The classification concerns that ambiguity, not a definite promise of convergence for arbitrary finite stopping rules, and does not require a new optimisation-error theorem.
